entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.desc: Japan's #1 company by market cap as of June 2026 (¥47.2T, +73% YTD), displacing Toyota. ARM Holdings (~90% stake) accounts for ~60% of NAV. Launched sovereign AI cloud platform for Japanese government ministries and regulated institutions — NVIDIA H100 clusters in Tokyo & Osaka. Lead sponsor of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (30-firm consortium, ¥1T NEDO backing). Masayoshi Son chairs the physical AI initiative.

entities.name: NEC Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's largest system integrator. Anthropic's first Japan-based Global Partner; deploying Claude Opus across ~30,000 NEC Group engineers via BluStellar Scenario platform. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Runs dual-stack hedge: backs sovereign domestic model while distributing Claude for enterprise and government — SOC services for finance, manufacturing, and local government sectors.

entities.name: Fujitsu
entities.desc: Japan's largest IT services company. Dual frontier AI partnerships: Anthropic (Claude for government system integration) and OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise + Codex for 100,000 employees). Kozuchi platform + Takane LLM for enterprise deployment. 'Customer Zero' strategy: internal deployment before client rollout. METI sovereign AI infrastructure positioning. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. Rapidus investor.

entities.name: Sony AI
entities.desc: Sony Group AI subsidiary. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Research focus covers robotics, gaming AI, and imaging intelligence. Sony's hardware ecosystem (PlayStation, cameras, sensors) provides unique data sources for physical AI training.

entities.name: Preferred Networks (PFN)
entities.zh: プリファードネットワークス
entities.desc: Tokyo-based AI startup; PLaMo LLM, robotics control software. Contributing engineers to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV on secondment. Japan's leading pure-play AI research company with deep industrial partnerships.

entities.name: NTT Research
entities.desc: Research arm of NTT Group (日本電信電話). Quantum and AI research; Rapidus investor in ¥267.6B funding round. NTT is Japan's national telecom incumbent — provides critical infrastructure for data center connectivity underpinning Japan's AI ambitions.

entities.name: Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co.
entities.zh: 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発
entities.desc: Japan's sovereign physical AI consortium. Founded by SoftBank, NEC, Sony, Honda. ~30 firms committed as of June 2026 including Honda, Nippon Steel, MUFG, Mizuho, Yaskawa, Fanuc, Asahi Kasei. Target: 1T-parameter model trained on Japanese sensor/robotics/manufacturing data (物理AI). ¥1T NEDO backing (grant, not equity). METI designated as national infrastructure — export-control carve-outs for compute hardware.

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed 2nm foundry. ¥267.6B raised (¥100B IPA + ¥167.6B private: Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, Fujifilm, 32 investors). Gov holds 11.5% + golden share (黄金株). IIM-1 in Chitose, Hokkaido: active 2nm GAA pilot line in FY2026. PDK general release to customers FY2026 (commercial activation milestone). Chiplet packaging (RCS) operational. Mass production target: FY2027. Confirmed clients: Fujitsu, Tenstorrent. CEO: Koike Atsuyoshi (小池淳義). NEDO FY2026 plan approved; second ¥631.5B tranche from METI.

entities.name: TSMC JASM (Kumamoto)
entities.desc: TSMC-majority JV in Kumamoto, Kyushu. Partners: Sony Group, Toyota, Denso. JASM-1: 6–12nm, production ramping 2024. JASM-2: upgraded to 3nm (approved April 2026), $17B total investment, government covers ~50%. Production target: 2028. Positions Kyushu as Japan's high-end semiconductor cluster alongside Rapidus Hokkaido. Serves automotive AI chip demand (Toyota, Honda, Denso supply chain).

entities.name: Kioxia
entities.desc: Japan's leading NAND flash memory manufacturer. Yokkaichi + Kitakami (北上) fabs. Cost per wafer ~$2,000 vs ~$4,000 Samsung, ~$6,000 Micron/SK Hynix — structural advantage through BiCS9. UBS initiated with Buy at ¥79,000 target (May 2026). Entire 2026 NAND output sold out. Q2 operating profit projected ¥1.3T — above full-year FY2025 record. BiCS10 (332-layer) will equalize cost advantage; UBS calls it a 12–18-month trade window. VLSI June 14: MSA-CBA 1,000-layer NAND demonstration.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
entities.desc: Japan's largest semiconductor equipment maker. Critical supplier of etch, deposition, and cleaning equipment to TSMC, Samsung, Rapidus. Under pressure from US export controls on advanced tool categories. Key beneficiary of Japan's semiconductor manufacturing renaissance.

entities.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
entities.desc: World's largest silicon wafer producer; critical input to TSMC Kumamoto and Rapidus Hokkaido. Also Japan's leading PVC producer. Semiconductor wafer division provides ~70% of silicon wafers used by leading-edge foundries globally.

entities.name: Fanuc
entities.desc: Japan's largest industrial robot and CNC machine maker. May 2026: announced Google Gemini integration enabling natural-language factory control — all future Fanuc robots will be compatible with Google software. Consortium member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. METI physical AI initiative beneficiary. Key robotics data contributor for Japan's sovereign 物理AI model.

entities.name: Yaskawa Electric
entities.desc: Tier-one industrial robot and servo-motor manufacturer. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV — servo and motion data key input to physical AI training. Along with Fanuc, represents Japan's dominance in industrial robotics (Japan controls ~70% of global industrial robot manufacturing).

entities.name: JAL × GMO Humanoid Trial (Haneda)
entities.zh: JAL × GMO AI＆ロボティクス
entities.desc: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics launched a two-year Unitree G1 humanoid robot trial at Haneda Airport in 2026 for baggage, cargo, and cabin operations. First cycle-time data from week of June 1. METI June liability guidelines will be the policy gate determining how quickly pilots convert into scaled commercial operations.

entities.name: Honda Motor
entities.desc: Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). First designated external deployer of the sovereign physical AI model. Long AI/robotics history (ASIMO humanoid). AI Foundation Model Consortium capital round closing June 2026. Woven City (Toyota JV) adjacent AI infrastructure investment.

entities.name: Nippon Steel
entities.desc: Japan's largest steelmaker. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV consortium (June 2026 capital round). Materials science data (steel properties, processing conditions) key training input for physical AI foundation model. Represents heavy industry capital backing Japan's sovereign AI ambitions.

entities.name: Asahi Kasei
entities.desc: Diversified chemicals and advanced-materials group. Investor in Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. Advanced materials data (fiber composites, chemical properties) adds manufacturing-floor sensor diversity to the physical AI training corpus.

entities.name: MUFG (Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group)
entities.desc: Japan's largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized to deploy dual AI cyber stack: Anthropic Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 in tandem. Part of FSA working group on AI-related cyber risks (36 entities, 15 critical infrastructure sectors). Each 25bp BOJ rate hike adds ~¥100–150B in annual net interest income across the three megabanks.

entities.name: Mizuho Financial Group
entities.zh: みずほフィナンシャルグループ
entities.desc: Japan's third-largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized for dual Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 AI cyber stack. BOJ rate normalization is structurally bullish for NII expansion.

entities.name: SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking)
entities.desc: Japan's second-largest bank. Government-authorized for dual AI cyber stack alongside MUFG and Mizuho. FSA working group participant. BOJ rate hike of 25bp adds ~¥100–150B NII across the three megabanks.

entities.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
entities.desc: Japan's central bank. Governor: Kazuo Ueda (植田和男). Policy rate: 0.75% (held April 2026, 6–3 vote split). Raised FY2026 core CPI forecast to 2.8% from 1.9%. OIS pricing June 2026: 77% probability of 25bp hike to 1.00% at June 15–16 MPM. Three dissenters favoured immediate hike. OECD projects 2.0% by end-2027. JGB purchase commitment signal at June MPM is the key 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' watch.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
entities.desc: Japan's fiscal authority. Finance Minister: Satsuki Katayama. Authorized record ¥11.73T (~$74B) FX intervention (為替介入) April 28–May 27, 2026 — first since July 2024, surpassing prior monthly record. USD/JPY hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. Issued fresh verbal warnings June 2026. 300bp US-Japan rate gap drives structural yen carry trade pressure.

entities.name: METI (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
entities.desc: Japan's industrial policy ministry. Designated Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. as national infrastructure (export-control carve-outs for compute hardware). Administering ¥1T NEDO AI fund (FY2026–FY2031). Overseeing Rapidus as national project. ¥6.7T subsidy framework for physical AI. Coordinated JASM TSMC Kumamoto 3nm upgrade subsidies. June 2026: publishing AI liability guidelines for humanoid robot deployments.

entities.name: NEDO
entities.zh: 新エネルギー・産業技術総合開発機構
entities.py: Shin'enerugī Sangyō Gijutsu Sōgō Kaihatsu Kikō
entities.desc: New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization. Executing Japan's ¥1T AI fund (FY2026–FY2031). Approved Rapidus FY2026 plan (PDK general release + chiplet pilot). Expected FY2026 budget allocation for Rapidus 2nm delayed from May, now due June week 1. Administers public-private designation for Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV.

entities.name: Digital Agency (デジタル庁)
entities.desc: Japanese government agency overseeing national digitization. Key AI deployment customer for Fujitsu's sovereign stack and NEC's system integration services. Procurement requiring domestically operated AI benefits Fujitsu's dual-provider positioning.

entities.name: FSA (Financial Services Agency)
entities.desc: Japan's financial regulator. Launched public-private working group on AI-related cyber risks: 36 entities across 15 critical infrastructure sectors. Authorized Japan's three megabanks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) to deploy dual AI cyber stack (Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5). AI cyber governance framework in development.
